q: On which date was the Constitution of India adopted by the Constituent Assembly?
e: The Constitution was adopted on 26 November 1949 and came into force on 26 January 1950.

q: Who was the Chairman of the Drafting Committee of the Constituent Assembly?
e: Dr. B. R. Ambedkar chaired the Drafting Committee; B. N. Rau was the Constitutional Advisor.

q: The Fundamental Duties of citizens are listed in which Part of the Constitution?
e: Fundamental Duties are in Part IV-A (Article 51A), added by the 42nd Amendment.

q: Which Article gives the Right to Constitutional Remedies, allowing citizens to move the Supreme Court?
e: Article 32 lets a person approach the Supreme Court directly to enforce Fundamental Rights.

q: What is the minimum age required to be elected President of India?
e: Article 58 requires a presidential candidate to have completed 35 years of age.

q: Who is the ex-officio Chairman of the Rajya Sabha?
e: Under Article 64, the Vice-President is the ex-officio Chairman of the Rajya Sabha.

q: Fundamental Rights are contained in which Part of the Indian Constitution?
e: Part III (Articles 12 to 35) deals with Fundamental Rights.

q: The words 'Socialist' and 'Secular' were added to the Preamble by which Amendment?
e: The 42nd Amendment (1976) added Socialist, Secular and Integrity to the Preamble.

q: Who is the Supreme Commander of the Indian Armed Forces?
e: Article 53 vests the supreme command of the defence forces in the President.

q: Article 17 of the Constitution deals with:
e: Article 17 abolishes untouchability and forbids its practice in any form.

q: Which Constitutional Amendment gave constitutional status to Panchayati Raj institutions?
e: The 73rd Amendment (1992) added Part IX on Panchayats; the 74th dealt with municipalities.

q: The Governor of a state is appointed by:
o: The Chief Justice of the High Court
e: Under Article 155, the President appoints the Governor by warrant under his hand and seal.

q: The idea of Directive Principles of State Policy was borrowed from the Constitution of:
e: India borrowed the concept of DPSP from the Irish Constitution.

q: Which Article of the Constitution defines a 'Money Bill'?
e: Article 110 defines a Money Bill; Article 112 is about the annual financial statement (Budget).

q: Who presides over a joint sitting of both Houses of Parliament?
e: Under Article 118(4), the Speaker of Lok Sabha presides over a joint sitting held under Article 108.

q: A National Emergency can be proclaimed under which Article?
e: Article 352 deals with National Emergency; 356 is President's Rule and 360 is Financial Emergency.

q: Right to Education (Article 21A) was inserted by which Amendment?
e: The 86th Amendment (2002) made free and compulsory education for children aged 6-14 a Fundamental Right.

q: The provisions related to anti-defection are contained in which Schedule?
e: The Tenth Schedule, added by the 52nd Amendment (1985), contains the anti-defection law.

q: Right to Property was removed from the list of Fundamental Rights by the:
e: The 44th Amendment made property a legal right under Article 300A.

q: Which writ is issued to free a person from illegal detention?
e: Habeas Corpus means 'to have the body'; the court orders the detained person to be produced.

q: Who administers the oath of office to the President of India?
e: Under Article 60, the Chief Justice of India administers the oath to the President.

q: The Comptroller and Auditor General of India is provided for under which Article?
e: Article 148 provides for the CAG; Article 76 is for the Attorney General.

q: What is the quorum required to hold a meeting of either House of Parliament?
e: Article 100 fixes the quorum at one-tenth of the total number of members of the House.

q: Who finally decides whether a Bill is a Money Bill or not?
e: Article 110(3) makes the Speaker's decision on a Money Bill final.

q: The 12th Schedule, listing the functions of municipalities, was added by which Amendment?
e: The 74th Amendment (1992) added Part IX-A and the 12th Schedule with 18 subjects for municipalities.

q: The voting age in India was reduced from 21 to 18 years by which Amendment?
e: The 61st Amendment Act, 1988 lowered the voting age to 18 years.

q: The 'basic structure' doctrine was laid down by the Supreme Court in which case?
e: In Kesavananda Bharati (1973), the Court held that Parliament cannot alter the basic structure of the Constitution.

q: Which Article empowers the President to establish an Inter-State Council?
e: Article 263 provides for an Inter-State Council; Article 262 deals with inter-state water disputes.

q: Who chaired the Union Powers Committee of the Constituent Assembly?
e: Nehru headed the Union Powers, Union Constitution and States Committees; Patel headed the Provincial Constitution Committee.

q: Under Article 360, the President can proclaim:
e: Article 360 deals with Financial Emergency, which has never been declared in India so far.
